title: Every Relayer operation is gated by the same three preconditions: role, active flag, and rate limit
content:
The function signatures quoted throughout A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2 share a shape. `mintUSDS`, `burnUSDS`, `swapUSDSToUSDC`, `swapUSDCToUSDS` and `transferUSDCToCCTP` are each declared `onlyRole(RELAYER)` and `isActive`, and each is followed by a `rateLimited(...)` clause naming the relevant limit. The generic ERC-4626 and Aave procedures repeat the same three preconditions in prose: "Spark Liquidity Layer contract `isActive`, ALM Proxy has sufficient underlying asset, and the ... amount is within instance-specific `RateLimits`."

The uniformity is what makes the security model comprehensible. Three orthogonal questions — *who* is asking, *is the system running*, and *is there capacity* — are answered at every entry point, so no operation can accidentally omit one.

The `isActive` modifier is the mechanism behind the Freezer role. A freeze does not have to be applied venue by venue or limit by limit: flipping one flag causes every Relayer entry point to reject, atomically and completely. That is why a single Freezer Multisig can halt the whole Liquidity Layer across a chain, and why the emergency response is fast enough to be worth having.

The design lesson is that a uniform guard triple is a stronger property than any individual limit. Adding a new Controller function means satisfying the same three checks, so the safety envelope extends to new integrations by construction rather than by review.
description: Each Controller function carries onlyRole(RELAYER), isActive, and a rateLimited check — so authorization, the global freeze and capacity are enforced uniformly rather than per integration.
